required_gaps: Correct and cover unregistered cleanup, companion replacement during a save lease, reserve-cache lifetime, and legacy alias recovery for a temporarily ineligible party rider. Obtain the focused receipt on the corrected commit.
source_inspection_only: The four findings below follow from production control flow. They were not reproduced in the game.
The city issues share a capital roster transition. Toolbar loss follows temporary control-fact withdrawal, while missing portraits follow the native roster's in-game pet filter.
The combat change handles explicit orders on already-unconscious living enemies. The conscious-trip case has a source trace, and the owner's original weapon and target state remain unknown.

findings.actual: ClearReserveBindings calls CountManagedHotbarSlots and ClearManagedHotbarSlots without a registration guard. Both pass a null blueprint to ResolveKind for a non-ability slot. ResolveKind compares by ReferenceEquals, so null matches an uninitialized control field. Cleanup then writes an empty slot over the unrelated shortcut. CaptureAndClearManagedHotbarSlots uses the same classification when scanning reserve bars for serialization.
findings.blocking_rationale: The expanded cleanup can erase player-authored reserve toolbar contents, which a subsequent save can make permanent.
findings.expected: Only a slot with an identifiable KMC blueprint is eligible for cleanup.
findings.requested_correction: Make ResolveKind return None for a missing input blueprint before comparing it with registered controls. Apply that identity rule to both cleanup and serialization.
findings.requested_evidence: Exercise reserve disable/disposal and save-scope capture before full registration with an occupied non-ability slot and an ordinary ability. Verify both original slot objects survive. Include a positive control for an exact registered KMC binding.
findings.title: Reserve cleanup can erase unrelated shortcuts before control registration completes
findings.trigger: Disable or dispose the service with a populated reserve roster before TryRegister succeeds, or after partial registration. A reserve bar contains an item or another non-ability shortcut.

findings.actual: EndSaveSerializationScope runs Update, which retires A's arrangement and can lease a fresh public fact for B. ClearSerializationHotbarLeases then checks only the old placeholder and the currently active blueprint fact. It restores B's data at A's index and calls ObserveBound, undoing the retirement.
findings.blocking_rationale: A save-scope lease can recreate a shortcut that reconciliation correctly retired and cause the next save to preserve it for the replacement companion.
findings.expected: A lease restores the chosen slot only while that arrangement still belongs to the rider's current companion. Genuine replacement retires it.
findings.requested_correction: Check the current public-control arrangement and companion identity when releasing a serialization lease. Preserve ordinary same-companion restoration and the existing placeholder check.
findings.requested_evidence: Lease slot 9 for pet A, change the rider's link to supported pet B before scope release, then run the production release order. Verify slot 9 stays empty and the next archive omits its kind-6 row. Repeat with A retained and verify exactly one binding at 9.
findings.title: Save-scope release can restore a retired shortcut for a different companion
findings.trigger: The public slot is leased for serialization, and the rider's companion changes from A to B before the save worker settles. The original placeholder remains in the slot.

acceptance_ids: §4 genuine companion removal and world disposal
findings.actual: reserveScanned is a strong HashSet of every reserve unit scanned in the world. No roster departure removes an entry. reserveScanWorld also strongly holds the Player, and AdmitReserveBindings returns on a null player before clearing either reference. The cache is released only on disable, service disposal or a later scan with another nonnull player.
findings.blocking_rationale: The new scan cache retains retired entity graphs for the continuing session and can retain a disposed world while no replacement player is present.
findings.expected: One-time migration bookkeeping releases removed unit instances and the disposed player world.
findings.requested_correction: Bound the scan bookkeeping to current roster membership and world lifetime, or use weak identities that cannot keep discarded units or the Player alive.
findings.requested_evidence: Scan a reserve unit, remove it from the roster, then dispose the world with no replacement player. Verify the service releases both identities. Retain a control showing repeated scans of an unchanged reserve bar do not repeat migration.
findings.title: Reserve scan bookkeeping retains removed units and the outgoing player world
findings.trigger: A scanned reserve unit permanently leaves the roster, or the world is disposed before another nonnull Player is scanned.

findings.actual: The new reserve recovery handles this alias, but the party reconciliation path converts it to an empty slot whenever publicActive is false and records placement as complete. Boundary observation recognizes only the canonical public blueprint. With no earlier arrangement, the alias index is lost and later reconciliation leaves the rider off the bar.
findings.blocking_rationale: An identifiable supported older shortcut is permanently lost on temporary pet non-resolution, depending on which roster handles the rider first.
findings.expected: An exact legacy Mount or Dismount binding preserves its recoverable index until the same pet resolves. An existing canonical binding takes precedence.
findings.requested_correction: Preserve the identifiable legacy index before clearing an unavailable party rider's alias, including when archive capture precedes the first update. Use the existing migration precedence and permanent-loss rules.
findings.requested_evidence: Start a party rider with a legacy alias at 9, no owned rows, and a persistent pet ID whose unit temporarily fails to resolve. Exercise update-first and save-first order. Verify a resave retains the index and the same pet's return restores the canonical control once. A cleared link should recover nothing.
findings.title: A temporarily unavailable party rider loses an older Mount or Dismount binding
findings.trigger: An older native bar has an exact legacy alias and no owned placement rows. The rider is a current candidate when first reconciled, but its linked pet is temporarily unresolved.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: RecoveredPublicSlot gives the canonical public binding precedence over legacy aliases. The reserve loop migrates legacy Mounted Charge through ResolveStockChargeForSlot and preserves an existing stock Charge elsewhere. The candidate gate records the mixed-bar regression passing.

Live, unbound reconciliation now preserves the interrupted slot and known companion identity when the pet link is empty but the relationship still grants Dismount. The candidate gate records the faulted-rider regression passing, including the entitlement-ended and different-pet controls.

summary.delivered_behavior: The candidate adds per-rider placement intent using the existing archive format, projects eligible reserve owners' persistent pets into the capital UI roster, and carries an explicit order on an already-unconscious living enemy through mounted attack admission. Both pending round-eight corrections pass their focused regressions.
remaining_owner_review: After correction, verify chosen-slot persistence through actual capital visits and saves, and inspect and equip the exact reserve pet in Inventory and Character.
